mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 5.0% signals a tightening monetary cycle that increases discount rates on equity cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% signals tightening labor market conditions that increase wage pressures and inflation expectations, prompting central bank hawkishness and reducing equity valuations over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases when UNRATE < 4.5%, or the Rank IC over any 3-year window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts above 1.6 million units signals strong consumer demand and confidence, which drives corporate revenue expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST > 1600.0, or the Rank IC over any 3-year window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production below 110.0 indicates weakening real economic activity and reduced corporate output, which lowers earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases when INDPRO < 110.0, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and residential fixed investment (RSAFS) signals broad-based demand strength that supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
